purpose: Identity pin for the WASI 0.2 component probe binaries that the dated security evidence cites.
policy: The four .wasm files listed here are BUILD ARTIFACTS and are not committed: .gitignore excludes *.wasm and does not carry an exception for this directory.
Any document that cites one of them as the fixture of a measurement therefore cites a byte sequence identified by the sha256 below, not a file that a clone contains.
Rebuild with ./rebuild.sh (needs cargo with the wasm32-wasip2 target plus wasm-tools). The script compares each rebuilt artifact against this manifest and fails on drift.

A hash mismatch after a rebuild is not permission to record a new hash. The measurements below were taken with THESE bytes; a different binary is a different experiment and the measurement has to be re-run and re-dated.
not_a_reproducibility_promise: These hashes pin WHICH bytes a cited measurement ran on. They do not claim that any toolchain reproduces them: rustc/WASI-binding revisions change codegen, and the toolchain revision used for each historical build was not recorded in the artifact. Reproducible-in-principle is stated per fixture as source + build command; byte-identical-in-practice is not claimed.
verification: tests/test_component_probe_fixtures.py — checks this manifest against the scripts and the documentation, and against the real bytes whenever they are present on disk.
